Ireland – Railway construction works – TII499 Luas Finglas Main Infrastructure Design and Construction Works
description: Luas Finglas is a 4 km extension of the Luas Green Line, delivering a high-capacity light rail connection between Finglas and Dublin city centre to support sustainable transport and urban development. The scheme will serve communities including Charlestown, Finglas Village, Finglas West, St Helena’s, and the Tolka Valley, and will comprise four new stops at St Helena’s, Finglas Village, St Margaret’s Road, and Charlestown. It also includes a 350-space Park and Ride facility near St Margaret’s Road, as well as interchange opportunities with bus services and with mainline rail services at Broombridge. The Luas Finglas Main Infrastructure Design and Construction Works will be delivered under the NEC4 Engineering and Construction Contract (ECC) Option C (Target Cost with Activity Schedule). The scope of this Contract (TII-499) includes, but is not limited to, the design and construction of the following principal elements: 1. Site clearance and demolitions. 2. Track (trackbed and rails). 3. Luas Stops at St Helena’s, Finglas Village, St Margaret’s Road and Charlestown. 4. Broombridge stabling site works. 5. Park and Ride facilities at St Margaret's Road. 6. Royal canal and rail overbridge at Broombridge. 7. Tolka Valley Park Bridge. 8. Fencing, retaining walls, boundary treatments and accommodation work. 9. Utility services realignment, diversion, replacement, and protection. 10. Road realignments and junction modifications. 11. Pedestrian and cycling facilities including cycle storage structures. 12. Road traffic signalling. 13. Landscape and urban realm upgrades. 14. Overhead Catenary System (OCS). 15. Power and Systems infrastructure. 16. Signalling, controls and other rail systems. 17. Working in live traffic environment on the busiest radial corridors in the greater Dublin area including property and business frontage reconfiguration. 18. Heritage / archaeology mitigation works. 19. Installation of stop furniture. 20. Installation of Validators and Ticket Vending Machines. 21. Other Ancillary works. The successful Contractor will also be responsible for: • Overall systems integration. • Interfacing and co-ordinating with other works packages to facilitate completion of works. • Interfacing and co-ordinating with stakeholders. • Testing and commissioning.

title: Unison
description: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) is soliciting innovative proposals for Unison, a program to develop and evaluate collaborative-autonomy approaches that jointly adapt team decision-making and communications during mission execution. Unison will investigate approaches that enable autonomous teams to modify tactics, behaviors, coordination relationships, and information exchange as mission complexity and operational variability increase and communications become constrained and/or degraded (see Section 7, Glossary, for program-specific definitions of terms in italics). The core hypothesis of Unison is that a unified execution-time reasoning approach to action planning and communications planning can improve the effectiveness, scalability, and resilience of collaborative autonomy in dynamic, uncertain, and resource-constrained environments. Unison seeks to preserve mission performance while reducing communication dependence and bounding the reasoning burden imposed on individual agents. Unison frames collaborative autonomy as a multi-agent decision problem in which agents use local observations, mission context, relevance, and mission objectives to select a policy that jointly defines physical actions and communications actions. At each decision point, the team must determine what actions to take, which coordination relationships must be maintained, and what information must be exchanged to preserve the coordination required for mission success. Unison will investigate approaches across teams of tens to hundreds of agents operating in representative collaborative, multi-domain mission scenarios.

title: HYDROSPHERE, BIOSPHERE, & GEOPHYSICS (HBG) SUPPORT SERVICES II - FINAL REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (FRFP)
description: The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC), hereby invites interested parties to review the Final Request for Proposal (FRFP) for the Hydrosphere, Biosphere, and Geophysics (HBG) Support Services II requirement supporting the Earth Sciences Division (ESD) at NASA/GSFC. The principal purpose of this requirement is to provide science research that conceives, develops, and applies space, field-deployed (i.e. airborne and in situ) and laboratory based technologies and observations to address issues of importance to society. These include but are not limited to water resources, land and ocean ecosystems, global and regional sea level change, changes in the Earth�s cryosphere, gravity field, magnetic field, solid Earth, and the terrestrial reference frame. The Statement of Work, Attachment A, describes the scope of the requirement. This contract is for support of a full range of science and research activities across the breadth of the various Laboratories that make up the HBG sub-division: the Cryospheric Sciences, Ocean Ecology, Hydrological Sciences, Biospheric Sciences, and Geodesy and Geophysics Laboratories. This contract is also for support of science, research and computing activities within the Terrestrial Information Systems Laboratory (TISL), also in the ESD. For the purposes of this document and contract the term HBG will be used to encompass all the Laboratories of the HBG sub-division and the TISL. NASA will conduct this acquisition as a small business set-aside. This competitive acquisition was originally contemplated as a Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee (CPFF), Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract with the ability to issue CPFF task orders. Following further acquisition planning and assessment of the Government's requirements, the contract structure has been modified. The HBG II Draft Request for Proposal (DRFP) posted on April 8, 2025 was issued as an IDIQ CPFF solicitation. As amended, this competitive acquisition will now result in a HYBRID Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) with the ability to issue Cost Plus Fixed Fee (CPFF) AND Firm- Fixed Price (FFP) task orders. The contract will have an effective ordering period of five years from the contract effective date. Interested offerors are encouraged to review the solicitation and all associated attachments for complete details regarding the requirements and proposal submission instructions. Please see the attached cover letter for additional information.

title: Y1JZ--Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Design-Build & Construction Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC) National VA Healthcare Construction Program
description: The VA requires multiple indefinite-delivery, indefinite- quantity (IDIQ) Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC) type contracts to provide construction services enterprise wide. The objective of this procurement is to award multiple IDIQ MATOCs for construction services nationwide within specified pools. These pools will meet the VA infrastructure needs for construction, renovation, maintenance, and repair within the 50 United States and its territories. title: Fuels Management Services at Malmstrom Air Force Base, MT and FE Warren Air Force Base, WY
description: Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Energy is issuing a Request for Proposal (RFP) for fuels operations and management to include bulk storage services, retail service station support, alongside aircraft services, and entire fuels management services at two Government-Owned, Contractor-Operated (GOCO) facilities, Malmstrom Air Force Base (AFB), MT and FE Warren AFB, WY. The Contractor will ensure safe, accurate, and timely handling, quality control, and accountability of all Defense-Wide Working Capital Fund (DWCF)-owned petroleum products under their control. The Contractor will perform required maintenance to ensure facilities, associated systems, vehicles, and equipment remain operational to meet the base mission. The Contractor shall provide sufficient general-purpose vehicles with appropriate capability to meet the contract requirements but not limited to escorting fuel deliveries where required, towing bowsers, transporting personnel, and performing expeditor duties as needed. The Contractor should provide sufficient special purpose vehicles with appropriate capability to meet the contract requirements for aviation and ground product services. The Contractor will comply with environmental protection, safety, and security directives. The Contractor will conduct required training to ensure personnel are fully qualified to perform Performance Work Statements (PWS) tasks. Tasks identified in the PWS are performed by either the Contractor or Agency as specified in Appendix M The Contractor is responsible for staffing, operations, maintenance, safety, security, environmental protection, training, contractor-furnished items, and Contractor Detailed Plans related to the fuel operations at the location. The Contractor shall conduct all necessary fuels operations to support base operations, airshows and special events, deployments, exercises, and contingencies under normal conditions, as well as, during periods of heightened security, inclement weather, or other unique situations. Operations must be safely and efficiently conducted to receive, store, transfer, issue, and account for fuel products with appropriate controls to ensure fuel quality, inventory accuracy, and no environmental impact. The Contractor shall operate and maintain the self-service automated service station facilities, equipment, and systems and ensure sufficient product is available to provide 24 hours a day, seven days a week support of ground fuels. The Contractor shall perform required tasks to ensure fuel is properly accounted for and issued to only authorized users. This procurement will be 100% restricted to Service Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) participation. Firms submitting a proposal under this RFP must be certified as SDVOSB by the Small Business Administration in accordance with FAR 19.1403. The NAICS Code is 493190 (Other Warehouse and Storage). The Government anticipates awarding two firm fixed-price contracts. This requirement will be for a four-year base period (April 1, 2027 to March 31, 2031), a five-year option period (April 1, 2031 to March 31, 2036), and an option to extend the contract for up to six individual months (April 1, 2036 to September 30, 2036). This procurement will be solicited under full and open competition after exclusion of sources. Interested firms may submit proposals for one location or both locations. The solicitation will be published electronically on the SAM website at https://sam.gov/. Interested companies responding to the solicitation will be required to register in the System for Award Management (SAM) and Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) prior to submitting a proposal. The Date of the Pre-Preproposal conference, in conjunction with the sites visit will be listed in the solicitation. Offerors will be required to submit in writing to the Contract Specialist (via e-mail) the name(s) and email(s) of the individual(s) who plan to attend by 11:00 AM Eastern Time on October 22, 2026.

title: Request for Proposals (RFP) for Fresh Fruit & Vegetable support for DLA Troop Support's DoW Troop and Non-DoW School and Indian Tribal Organization customers located in Dallas, TX
description: The DLA Troop Support intends to solicit a full-line of produce support for DoD (Troop) customers and Non-DoD (USDA School & Indian Tribal Organization) customers located in the Dallas, Texas Zone. This acquisition will be issued on a small business set-aside (100%) basis. A waiver of the Non-Manufacturer rule has not been requested for this acquisition because it is an acquisition for multiple items. In accordance with 13 CFR 121.406(d)(1), if at least 50% of the estimated contract value of an acquisition for multiple items is composed of items that are manufactured by small business concerns, then a waiver of the Non-Manufacturer rule is not required. As such, for this acquisition, it is expected that items comprising at least 50% of the contract value will be manufactured by small business concerns. The contracting officer must be immediately notified if it appears as though this requirement will not be met. The total length of the contract will be five (5) years. It contains one (1) twenty-four (24) month tier, and two (2) eighteen (18) month tiers. Its estimated maximum total contract dollar value is $243,976,437.00. The delivery points require indefinite quantities of Fresh Fruit and Vegetables throughout the term of the contract. A more detailed listing of the delivery sites can be found in the solicitation. All responsible sources may submit proposals that will be considered by DLA Troop Support. The Government will award a contract(s) resulting from this solicitation to the responsible offeror(s) whose offer(s) conforming to the solicitation will be most advantageous to the Government, price and other factors considered. The source selection method for this procurement will be the Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) source selection procedures and shall use the following to evaluate offers: 1. Technical Acceptability - A technically acceptable offer is an offer that takes no exceptions to the terms and conditions in the solicitation and complies fully with all submission requirements, including submissions relating to the two subfactors listed below. A proposal that takes exception to solicitation terms and conditions or that fails to comply with all submission requirements may be deemed technically unacceptable and, thus, may be found ineligible, and removed from further consideration for the award. By submitting a proposal with no exceptions, an offeror is confirming it possesses the necessary facilities, equipment, technical skills and capacity to successfully provide all items required by this solicitation. The following sub-factors will be evaluated and must be found acceptable for a proposal to be eligible for award: A. Perishable Agricultural Commodities Act (PACA) License - The offeror shall possess and submit proof of a valid current PACA license. B. USDA Harmonized Good Agricultural Practices (GAP) Plus + Standard Audit with warehouse and food defense addenda and/or USDA Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) audit - The Contracting Officer will require an offeror to submit a valid USDA Harmonized GAP Plus + Standard audit, including addenda for warehouse and food defense, and/or USDA GMP audit, or an independent third-party certifying company audit report(s) / certificate for each place of performance identified in the offeror's proposal. The audit report(s) must demonstrate a passing score in the following parts: General, Warehouse and Food Defense addenda. In lieu of a USDA Harmonized GAP Plus + Standard and/or USDA GMP audit report / certificate, the offeror may submit an audit report / certificate conducted by a recognized private independent third-party certifying company certifying to an industry recognized food safety standard that exceeds all aspects of the USDA Harmonized GAP Plus + Standard audit and/or USDA GMP report / certificate requirements. Offerors relying on a non-USDA Harmonized GAP Plus + Standard and/or USDA GMP audit report / certificate that do not agree to have a USDA Harmonized GAP Plus + Standard and/or USDA GMP audit report / certificate for each place of performance prior to the start of contract performance will be found technically unacceptable. 2. Pricing - Pricing is required for all items found in the Schedule of Items (for Group 1 and 2 (2a and 2b), if applicable) and for all tiers. Failure to offer pricing for all items and for all tiers may result in a proposal being removed from consideration for award as technically unacceptable. The Government will perform an aggregate price analysis on all items found in the Schedule of Items (for Group 1 and 2 (2a and 2b), if applicable). To determine an offeror's Evaluated Aggregate Price for Group 1, the Weighted Aggregate Distribution Price will be added to the Aggregate Delivered Price. To determine an offeror's Evaluated Aggregate Price Group 2 (2a and 2b), the Weighted Aggregate Distribution Price will be added to the Aggregate Delivered Price for each sub-group 2a and 2b, respectively, to come to a preliminary Evaluated Aggregate Price for each sub-group. Then, the preliminary Evaluated Aggregate price for 2a and 2b will be added together to determine the offeror's Evaluated Aggregate Price for Group 2. Please refer to paragraph (d) below for further details regarding these price components. The award(s) will be made on the basis of the lowest Evaluated Aggregate Price (for each group) of proposals meeting or exceeding the acceptability standards for non-price factors. The Government reserves the right to remove item(s) from the Schedule of Items. Prior to award, the offered prices of the presumptive awardee(s) will be evaluated on an individual line-item basis to determine whether each price is fair and reasonable using analytical techniques deemed appropriate by the Contracting Officer in her/his complete discretion. A. Price Components: 1. Weighted Aggregate Distribution Price: Aggregate Distribution Price is obtained by first multiplying the proposed distribution price for each item in the Schedule of Items by the item's estimated quantity to calculate the total distribution price for each item. Then, the total distribution prices of all items will be added together to determine the total distribution price for tier 1. The total distribution price for each subsequent tier will also be calculated. The total distribution prices for all tiers will be added together to determine the Aggregate Distribution Price. The Aggregate Distribution Price is then multiplied by a weighting factor of 6 to arrive at the Weighted Aggregate Distribution Price. Note: the weighting factor is applied only to the overall Aggregate Distribution Price (not on a line item basis), and is to be used for evaluation purposes only. The Government's use of a weighting factor of 6 for distribution pricing is done in order to more accurately balance the significance of the pricing components and their respective impact on any subsequent contract(s) issued under this solicitation. 2. Aggregate Delivered Price: The Aggregate Delivered Price is obtained by first multiplying the proposed delivered price of each item in the Schedule of Items by the item's estimated quantity to calculate the total delivered price for each item. Then, the total delivered prices of all items will be added together to determine the total delivered price for tier 1. The total delivered price for each subsequent tier will also be calculated. The total delivered prices for all tiers will be added together to determine the Aggregate Delivered Price. 3. Evaluated Aggregate Price: The Evaluated Aggregate Price is obtained by adding the Weighted Aggregate Distribution Price and Aggregate Delivered Price together. 4. For purposes of the Price Proposal Evaluation, Weighted Aggregate Distribution Price and Aggregate Delivered Price are considered equal. This equality is accounted for mathematically by applying a weighting factor of 6 (based on current Government data) to the Aggregate Distribution Price. Option

description: Program Acquisition Executive Marine Corps (PAE MC) Program Manager Tactical Communications & Electromagnetic Warfare Systems (PM TCE) is assessing industry�s capability to provide Commercial-Off-The-Shelf (COTS) tactical camera systems, lenses, and accessories under a Hardware-as-a-Service (HaaS) operating lease model. Accidental trapping of mercury in a component could cause serious damage to vital parts. Mercury is also toxic if inhaled, ingested, or absorbed through the skin. When any change in design, material, servicing or part number is made to replace or substitute any item to be furnished on this contract/purchase order, the Contractor shall furnish, for the substituting/replacement item, a drawing and an explanation of the reason for the change, explaining the reason therefor. If finished detail drawings are not available, shop drawings in the form used by the manufacturer will be acceptable for Government evaluation. When notifying the Procurement Contracting Officer of the reasons for making substitutions, the type of change shall be indicated by code number in accordance with one of the following statements: Code 1: PART NUMBER CHANGE ONLY - If the Manufacturer's Part Number indicated thereon has changed, but the parts are identical in all respects, supply the item and advise NAVICP-MECH immediately of the new part number. Code 2: Assembly (or set or kit) not furnished - Used following detail parts. Code 3: Part not furnished separately - Use assembly. Code 4: Part redesigned - Old and new parts are completely interchangeable. Code 5: Part redesigned - New part replaces old. Old part cannot replace new. Code 6: Part redesigned - Parts not interchangeable. 3.4 Mercury Free - The material supplied under this contract/purchase order is intended for use on submarines/surface ships and therefore shall contain no metallic mercury and shall be free from mercury contamination. Mercury contamination of the material will be cause for rejection. If the inclusion of metallic mercury is required as a functional part of the material furnished under this contract, the Contractor shall obtain written approval from the Procurement Contracting Officer before proceeding with manufacture. The contractor's request shall explain in detail the requirements for mercury, identify specifically the parts to contain mercury, and explain the method of protection against mercury escape. Such a request will be forwarded directly to the Procurement Contracting Officer with a copy to the applicable Government Inspector. Upon approval by the Contracting Officer, the vendor will provide a "Warning Plate" stating that metallic mercury is a functional part of the item and will include name and location of that part. The use of mercury, mercury compounds, or mercury-bearing instruments and/or equipment in a manner which might cause contamination in the manufacture, assembly, or test of material on this contract is prohibited. The most probable causes of contamination are direct-connected manometers, mercury vacuum pumps, mercury seals, or the handling of mercury in the immediate vicinity. Mercury switches, mercury in glass thermometers, standard cells and other items containing mercury may be used if they are located so as not to constitute a contamination hazard. If external contamination by metallic mercury occurs or is suspected, the following test may be used to determine whether contamination by metallic mercury exists or whether corrective cleaning measures have been effective. Enclose the equipment in a polyethylene bag or close-fitting airtight container for eight hours at room temperature (70 degrees F minimum).Sample the trapped air and if mercury vapor concentration is 0.01 mg/cu meter or more, the material is mercury contaminated insofar as the requirements of this contract are concerned. These requirements shall be included in any subcontract or purchase order hereunder and the Contractor shall insure SubContractor compliance with these requirements. Technical questions pertaining to these requirements shall be referred to the Procurement Contracting Officer via the cognizant Administrative Contracting Officer. For background, the following information is provided: Mercury is corrosive to gold, silver, nickel, stainless steels, aluminum and copper alloys. Stainless steels, nickel, and copper alloys are widely used in reactor plants and other submarine/surface ship systems. Accidental trapping of mercury in a component could cause serious damage to vital parts. Mercury is also toxic if inhaled, ingested, or absorbed through the skin. It is evident that grave consequences could result from small amounts of mercury vapor present in an unreplenished submarine/surface ship atmosphere. 3.5 Additive Manufacturing- If/When Additive Manufacturing election taken by vendor, to maintain visibilityover Additively Manufactured components within the supply chain, Contract Data Requirements List (CDRL) DD1423 reporting mechanisms apply. title: FCI Oxford - Water Softener
description: The Federal Bureau of Prisons (FBOP) and the Federal Correctional Institution Oxford located at 350 Elk Avenue, Oxford, Wisconsin, intend to make a single award to a responsible entity that will provide all necessary equipment, labor, materials, and incidentals to remove existing water softeners and install a new centralized water softener for the entire Institution. Awarded Contractor shall provide materials, labor, and equipment to remove existing water softeners, pipe through and install a new centralized water softener and all associated components. FCI Oxford currently has several commercial-grade water softeners which are failing to efficiently reduce water hardness and protect water systems, as well as connected equipment. The new centralized system should improve water quality, minimize calcium buildup, and extend the service life of plumbing infrastructure and appliances. The contractor would place a brine tank and softener to be installed at the water tower. Water would be treated right off the water main, therefore there would be no need for bagged salt to be brought in weekly.

Please refer to the attachments section to access the updated documents. __________________________________________________________________________ The U.S. General Services Administration (GSA), Public Buildings Service, Capital Projects Contracting Division, is pleased to announce the issuance of a Request for Proposals (RFP) for a project at the Thurgood Marshall U.S. Courthouse, situated at 40 Foley Square in New York, NY. This project will include scope to modernize seventeen (17) elevators, as well as upgrade mechanical, electrical and fire protection equipment within the elevator machine rooms. The Courthouse will remain fully operational throughout the duration of the project. To ensure minimal disruption to Government operations, the work must be phased to limit interruptions to operations and any disruptive work must be executed after business hours, predominately work taking place within the elevator shaftways. The selected General Contractor will be required to ensure full compliance with the Government�s requirements for access and security. Additionally, the General Contractor will be required to complete this project in accordance with the construction drawings and specifications that will be issued for this project. The selected General Contractor will be required to ensure full compliance with the Public Buildings Service Interim Core Building Standards, and the U.S. Courts Design Guide. Contract Type: The contract type for this procurement will be Firm-Fixed price. The line item schedule will include a lump sum item for the Base. There will be option line items for this procurement. Price: The total magnitude of this project at award is between $20,000,000 and $40,000,000. Selection and Schedule: This requirement will be competitively procured in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 15.1�Source Selection Processes and Techniques ((GSA Class Deviation RFO-2025-15) and FAR 36.101-2 (GSA Class Deviation RFO-2025-36)). The awardee will be competitively chosen using best value tradeoff procedures in accordance with FAR Subparts 15.1 and 15.2 (GSA Class Deviation RFO-2025-15). NAICS: This procurement will be conducted under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code 236220--Commercial and Institutional Building Construction. The Small Business size standard is an average annual sales and receipts for the past three (3) years that are equal to or less than $45,000,000. All offerors are required to have an active registration in the System for Award Management (www.SAM.gov) at the time of offer submission, and shall continue to be registered until time of award, during performance, and through final payment of any contract. Proposals MUST BE RECEIVED NO LATER THAN stated due date and time in this solicitation. Inquiries concerning this solicitation must be routed to Contracting Officer Natalia Lugo-Vina at natalia.lugo-vinacruz.gsa.gov. Prospective offerors bear sole responsibility for tracking and retrieving the RFP alongside all associated amendments.

description: The Congressionally Directed Medical Research Programs (CDMRP) seeks feedback to inform the fiscal year 2027 (FY27) Alzheimer�s Research Program (AZRP) research focus areas and associated research funding opportunities. title: Bravo Dive Boat 65DS1101
description: AMENDMENT 0003 POSTED 11/26. AMENDMENT 0002 POSTED 11/21. AMENDMENT 0001 POSTED 11/19. The Regional Maintenance Center at Puget Sound Naval Shipyard & Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS & IMF) intends to award a stand-alone Firm-Fixed-Price contract to accomplish the maintenance, repair, and preservation in support of one (1) 65 FT BRAVO DIVE BOAT 65DS1101. Work will be accomplished at the Contractor's facility. Geographical Area of consideration: To facilitate proper government oversight, the facility shall be located in the Puget Sound, WA region. For this procurement, the Puget Sound, WA region is defined as the West Coast of the continental US, starting from Olympia, WA and extending northward to Bellingham, WA. 65DS1101 Length: 69 FT 10 IN Width: 22 FT 0 IN Draft: 3 FT 6 IN Full Displacement: 55 L TONS Age: 13 YEARS Light Load: 8,000 lbs Hull Type: Aluminum Scope Overview: Coordinate with the Contracting Officer, via the Contracting Officer�s Representative (COR) to deliver the vessel to the Contractor�s facility from Puget Sound Naval Shipyard (PSNS) Bremerton, WA. Remove all fendering and sweep blast clean. Accomplish survey of hull to identify and repair corrosion, preserve the exterior above and below the waterline, including the crane. Apply nonskid to horizontal surfaces on the exterior and interior of the boat. Replace motor mounts. Remove, inspect and install shafting, rudders and propellers. HVAC repair. Maintain and repair watertight hatches and doors. Repair, modify and preserve push knee. Replace and modify corroded deck and bulkhead structure in the main cabin. Install remote fuel shut offs. Identify and repair corrosion beneath the transformers in the aft lazzarette, install a weather shield above the starboard transformer in the aft lazzarette. Replace hydraulic, and fuel hoses. Identify and repair corroded structure beneath the shower room drain. Remove windows, repair window heaters, and reinstall windows. Replace fire suppression system piping and recertify system. Repair damage to the port bow. Accomplish modification and repair of swim platform stairs. Restore preservation system on the console in the pilot house. Replace existing generators with supplied Kohler generators, Modify, repair and install fendering system. Modify and repair the monkey heater system. Remove, inspect, preserve and install rudders. Replace thru hull valves and flexible hoses. Replace false bulkheads in the shower room and head. Open, clean and inspect all tanks. Perform sea trials after completion of repairs and full cure time of preservation. Arrange and coordinate the delivery of the vessel back to the Government with the Contracting Officer via the COR. title: C--Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) 3DNTM
description: This Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) is issued to provide an opportunity to partner with the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) and other Federal agencies to acquire high-resolution 3D elevation and hydrography mapping data through the 3DNTM Data Collaboration Announcement (DCA). The 3DNTM DCA partnerships efficiently and effectively leverage funding to respond to the documented and growing need for high-quality elevation and hydrography data, which significantly benefit Americans across an array of applications like infrastructure planning, discovery of critical minerals, energy development, and disaster preparation and response for severe weather events, earthquakes, landslides, and other emergencies. Project submissions are invited from applicants who wish to partner through the 3D Elevation Program (3DEP) opportunity or the 3D Hydrography Program (3DHP) opportunity to fund lidar or hydrography data acquisition through the USGS Geospatial Products and Services Contract (GPSC). Federal agencies, state and local governments, tribes, academic institutions, and the private sector are eligible to submit projects. The Government will review applications based on the evaluation criteria identified in section VII of this opportunity. A synopsis of previous 3DNTM DCA Awards is available on https://usgs.gov/3DNTM/DCA. 3DEP and 3DHP products and services, including data resulting from this opportunity can be accessed via The National Map Data Download and Visualization Services: https://apps.nationalmap.gov.

title: Versam, Ausbau BehiG - BKP 232 Elektroinstallationen
description:
Der Bahnhof Versam entspricht heute nicht den Anforderungen an das Behindertengleichstellungsgesetz und muss entsprechend umgebaut werden. Dazu wird am Haus- und Aussenperron ein BehiG-konformer Perron erstellt. Die beiden Perrons werden mit einer neuen Personenunterführung, inklusive Treppen und Lifte, erschlossen. Die Kreuzungsgleislänge wird vergrössert und die Gleisgeometrie entsprechend angepasst. Für die technischen Einrichtungen wird ein neues Dienstgebäude erstellt. Die Fahrleitungs-, Niederspannungs- und Sicherungsanlagen werden komplett erneuert. Die Hauptarbeiten sind für die Jahre 2027 und 2028 vorgesehen. Im Jahr 2026 erfolgten bauliche Vorbereitungs- und im Jahr 2028 die Abschlussarbeiten.

In diesem Los sind die Niederspannungs- und Telekominstallationen für den Neubau Versam gemäss Leistungsverzeichnis ausgeschrieben.

title: Port of Aalborg Logistics A/S - Udbud af hydraulisk kran 2026 - Offentligt udbud
description: Ovennævnte udbud af én (1) hydraulisk kran gennemføres af Servicemægleren A/S på vegne af Port of Aalborg Logistics A/S som et offentligt udbud med henblik på indgåelse af én kontrakt.Kranen skal leveres, installeres og idriftsættes på Kaj 8005 – Aalborg Havn – Landdybet, 9220 Aalborg Øst.Udbuddet omfatter indkøb af én (1) diesel/HVO-drevet hydraulisk kran på gummihjulsmonteret undervogn. Den skal fortrinsvis anvendes til losning og lastning af skibe og til håndtering af bulkvarer, stykgods, biomasse og skrot på Ordregivers havneområde. Formålet er hurtig og præcis håndtering, så havnens gennemløbshastighed er høj, og skibenes liggetid er kort. Skibene varierer i en størrelse fra 3.000 DWT til 10.000 DWT.Kravene til kranen fremgår af Bilag B – Kravspecifikation. Tilsvarende løsninger til det i kravspecifikationen anførte kan tilbydes, hvis de dokumenteres at give samme funktion, sikkerhed og kvalitet. Udbuddet er ikke opdelt i delaftaler.Leverancen omfatter kranen med tilhørende udstyr (to grabber på hhv. 5 m³ samt en 7 m³ med lukkede sider, en polygrab på 3 m³ til skrot inkl. bobcatkroge og løftekapacitet på 8t og en krogblok med rotatorfunktion, alle med centralsmøring og tilslutning til kranens hurtigskifte). Leverancen omfatter levering, installation, driftsprøve, idriftsættelse mv. Den omfatter også dokumentation, operatøruddannelse, support, softwareassurance, service- og reservedelsforsyning samt garanti.

title: Germany – Internet service providers ISP – (TNW) Markt Bad Steben - Gigabit-RL 2.0 (2025) - Auswahlverfahren einer Dienstleistungskonzession im Wirtschaftlichkeitslückenmodell für die Planung, Errichtung und den Betrieb eines Gigabit-Netzes
description: Verhandlungsverfahren mit Teilnahmewettbewerb entsprechend § 12 KonzVgV i.V.m. § 14 Abs. 2, Abs. 3 Nr. 2, Nr. 3 VgV, § 119 Abs. 5 GWB (zweistufiges Verhandlungsverfahren) zur Be- stimmung eines Netzbetreibers für die Planung, die Errichtung und den Betrieb eines Gigabit- Netzes im Wirtschaftlichkeitslückenmodell in den ausgeschriebenen Ausbaugebieten nach Maßgabe der Richtlinie "Förderung zur Unterstützung des Gigabitausbau der Telekommunikati- onsnetze in der Bundesrepublik Deutschland" vom 31.03.2023 in der Fassung der 2. Änderung vom 13.01.2025 (nachfolgend "Gigabit-RL 2.0"). Aufgrund gegebener Grenznähe nimmt der Konzessionsgeber Binnenmarktrelevanz an und führt das Auswahlverfahren europaweit durch, obwohl der Schwellenwert nach § 106 GWB nicht er- reicht oder überschritten wird. Wesentliche Grundlage des Verfahrens sind die "Rahmenregelung der Bundesrepublik Deutsch- land zur Unterstützung des flächendeckenden Aufbaus von Gigabitnetzen" vom 01.08.2024 (nachfolgend "Gigabit-RR 2.0"), die Richtlinie "Förderung zur Unterstützung des Gigabitausbaus der Telekommunikationsnetze in der Bundesrepublik Deutschland" vom 31.03.2023 in der Fas- sung der 2. Änderung vom 13.01.2025 (nachfolgend Gigabit-RL 2.0) sowie die Mitteilung der Eu- ropäischen Union "Leitlinien für staatliche Beihilfen zur Förderung von Breitbandnetzen" vom 31.01.2023 (2023/C 36/01). Die ausgeschriebenen Adressen des Erschließungsgebietes sind nach Ergebnis der Markterkun- dung förderfähige unterversorgte Adressen im Sinne der Gigabit-RL 2.0. Aus diesem Grund soll dort auf Basis dieses Auswahlverfahrens ein Gigabit-Netz als technologieneutrale Netzbezeich- nung (Netz mit einer Breitbandversorgung von mindestens 1 Gbit/s symmetrisch zu Spitzenlast- zeitbedingungen für alle Endnutzer der ausgeschriebenen Adressen) in den unterversorgten Gebieten errichtet werden, wobei sich die Up- und Downloadraten mindestens verdoppeln müs- sen. Auf die Vorgaben der "B-Leistungsbeschreibung" inkl. deren Anlagen wird ergänzend ver- wiesen. Der Konzessionsgeber ordnet den ausgeschriebenen "Vertrag über die Weiterleitung von Zuwen- dungen im Rahmen des Gigabitausbaus in der Marktgemeinde Bad Steben zum Zwecke der Pla- nung, der Errichtung und des Betriebs eines gigabitfähigen Breitbandnetzes im Wirtschaftlichkeitslückenmodell nach der Richtlinie "Förderung zur Unterstützung des Gi- gabitausbaus der Telekommunikationsnetze in der Bundesrepublik Deutschland - Gigabit-Richt- linie des Bundes 2.0 (Gigabit-RL 2.0)" als eine Dienstleistungskonzession i.S.d. § 105 Abs. 1 Nr. 2 GWB ein. Der Konzessionsgeber überträgt damit die ihm als Aufgabe der Daseinsvorsorge oblie- gende Realisierung der Versorgung der Bevölkerung mit Gigabitanschlüssen auf den Konzessi- onsnehmer, welcher das Nutzungsrecht am Gigabit-Netz erhält und die Vergütung für seine Tätigkeit in erster Linie durch die Entgelte der Endkunden erhält, während der Konzessionsgeber lediglich einen Zuschuss zur Deckung der gegebenenfalls ausgewiesenen Wirtschaftlichkeitslü- cke leistet, welcher nach § 105 Abs. 1 Nr. 2 GWB einer Dienstleistungskonzession nicht entge- gensteht. Der Schwerpunkt der Tätigkeit des Konzessionsnehmers liegt auf der Dienstleistung des Betreibens des Breitbandnetzes über den Zeitraum von mindestens sieben Jahren. Der Konzessionsgeber ordnet weiter das zu planende, zu bauende und zu betreibende Gigabit- Netz auch als ein "öffentliches Kommunikationsnetz" i.S.d. Bereichsausnahme gemäß § 149 Nr. 8 GWB ein, so dass der 4. Teil des GWB nicht zur Anwendung kommt. Soweit in den Unterla- gen des Auswahlverfahrens auf Normen des 4. Teils des GWB verwiesen wird, begründet dies keinen Anspruch auf deren Anwendbarkeit.

title: Belgium – Fire engines – Aankoop 2 Bosbrandwagens Type CCF
description: Hulpverleningszone Noord-Limburg beschikt over grote oppervlakten natuurgebieden (o.a. Nationaalpark Bosland) die elk jaar getroffen worden door natuurbranden (bos, heide,…). Deze ruwe terreinen vereisen gespecialiseerde voertuigen alle terrein om de manschappen, benodigde materiaal en vereiste bluswater ter plaatse te krijgen. Hulpverleningszone Noord-Limburg beschikt reeds over bosbrandvoertuigen type CCF en wil haar vloot uitbreiden met 2 bijkomende bosbrandvoertuigen type CCF 4x4 4.000 l, één voor de nieuwe brandweerpost Peer en één voor brandweerpost Lommel. Beide voertuigen zijn identiek. Het voertuig van brandweerpost Peer dient echter bijkomend uitgerust te worden met een sproeibalk en een systeem voor de dosering van zeep/detergent zodat dit voertuig buiten de winterperiode eveneens gebruikt kan worden voor kleine opdrachten “reinigen wegdek”. In het dossier zal eveneens een bepakkingslijst toegevoegd worden. De aanbieder dient hiervoor de eenheidsprijzen op te geven zodat i.f.v. het resterende budget het voertuig bijkomend uitgerust kan worden met brandbestrijdingsmaterialen. Overige materialen zullen door de Hulpverleningszone Noord-Limburg aangeleverd worden zodat de nodige ruimte voorzien kan worden tijdens de opbouw. De uniformiteit van inrichting van deze nieuwe voertuigen t.o.v. de reeds in gebruik zijnde CCF’s dient behouden te blijven (in samenspraak met de Hulpverleningszone tijdens de opbouw/inrichting). Al het voorgestelde materieel dient nieuw te zijn en elk element dient te voldoen aan de bijzondere interventievoorwaarden. De leverancier dient hiermee rekening te houden bij het voorstellen van het materieel. Het voertuig betreft een bosbrandwagen type CCF voor 4 personen. Het voertuig dient voorzien te zijn van een autoprotectiesysteem met een gereserveerde hoeveelheid water om in geval van nood de bemanning te kunnen beschermen. Het chassis moet van een goedgekeurd en gehomologeerd type zijn, aangepast aan het voertuigontwerp. Deze aanpassing wordt onderbouwd door een gewichtsberekening van het volledige concept, die bij de offerte wordt gevoegd. Bij levering zal het voertuig worden nagewogen. Indien het voertuig niet voldoet aan het vooropgestelde gewicht, kan dit aanleiding geven tot weigering van het product. Het aangeboden voertuig moet van het meest recente commerciële type zijn en geschikt zijn voor rijden en inzet op ruw terrein (oneffenheden in terrein, bospaden, losse zand, heuvels,…). Het voertuig moet op het moment van indiening van de offerte én bij levering volledig voldoen aan de geldende Europese en Belgische regelgeving.

title: Mill Creek Section 205 Flood Risk Management Improvements
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Walla Walla District, is seeking information from interested business concerns capable of performing a construction project entitled Mill Creek Section 205 Flood Risk Management Improvements. The work is located in and near the Cities of Walla Walla and College Place, Walla Walla County, Washington. The Mill Creek Flood Control Project begins approximately two miles east of downtown Walla Walla and extends approximately seven miles downstream near College Place at the Gose Street Bridge. One hundred percent performance and payment bonds will be required. In accordance with RFO FAR Clause 52.228-1, a bid guarantee will also be required. The estimated magnitude of construction is between $10,000,000 and $25,000,000. The anticipated North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 237990, Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction, with a corresponding small-business size standard of $45,000,000 in average annual receipts. This sources-sought notice is issued for market-research purposes only to identify business concerns with the capability to perform work of this nature, magnitude, and complexity. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION FOR BIDS OR PROPOSALS. This notice does not constitute a commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract. The Government will not reimburse respondents for costs associated with preparation or submission of responses. Responses will be used to assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition strategy, including whether a small-business set-aside is appropriate. Interested business concerns should submit the following information: 1. Capability Statement. Provide a statement expressing interest in this requirement and describing the firm's capability to perform work of the anticipated magnitude and complexity. Identify special qualifications, certifications, key personnel, self-performance capabilities, equipment, and any proposed teaming arrangements relevant to the summary scope of work. 2. Relevant Experience. Provide at least three projects completed within the past seven years that are similar in scope, complexity, and magnitude. For each project, provide: -- Project title and location; -- Customer/owner; -- Contract value; -- Period of performance; -- Brief description of the work performed; -- The firm's role, including prime contractor, joint-venture member, or subcontractor; -- Major work self-performed by the firm; and -- Point of contact, including name, title, telephone number, and email address. 3. Identify the firm's business size under NAICS 237990 and any applicable socioeconomic designations, including small business, Small Disadvantaged Business, 8(a), Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone) small business, Woman-Owned Small Business, Veteran-Owned Small Business, and Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business. 5. SAM Registration. Provide the firm's Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and confirm whether its System for Award Management registration is active. Submit responses by email to: Chandra Crow, Contract Specialist U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Walla Walla District Email: Chandra.D.Crow@usace.army.mil Responses are due no later than 3:00 p.m. Pacific Time, December 4, 2026. Summary of Scope of Work: The Mill Creek Flood Control Project provides flood-risk management for the City of Walla Walla and adjacent areas in Walla Walla County, Washington. The project includes upstream channel, concrete channel, and downstream channel sections. The anticipated construction work includes flood-risk-management improvements and repairs at multiple locations along and within the upstream and downstream Mill Creek channel sections. Work may include: -- Raising existing levees by up to approximately three feet at five locations; -- Landward enlargement of levees while maintaining 2H:1V side slopes; -- Placement of additional gabion revetment at one location; -- Placement of additional riprap at transition areas, including ramp-to-levee and levee-to-bridge-abutment transitions; -- Construction of new concrete walls and/or raising of existing concrete walls at levee and bridge-transition locations; -- Construction of a concrete access ramp; -- Removal of trees and vegetation along the landside levee toe; -- Removal and in-kind replacement of existing fencing, as necessary to perform the work; -- Removal of a ceiling section in a covered portion of the existing concrete channel; -- Reinforcement of an existing timber-plank-covered support wall within the channel below an existing building; and -- Stabilization of two existing concrete-channel-wall sections using soil anchors and shotcrete facing. Work will occur on Federal and non-Federal/private property. The anticipated project may require work-site access planning, coordination with affected property owners and utilities, traffic control, in-kind replacement of fencing and utilities as required, and work within or adjacent to the active channel. The project is intended to improve Mill Creek system capacity by raising levees in low-assurance areas and to improve system reliability by repairing and reinforcing the concrete channel through downtown Walla Walla. Desired Contractor Capabilities: Interested firms should demonstrate experience with comparable civil-works construction, including: -- Levee raising, embankment construction, earthwork, compaction, and slope construction; -- Cast-in-place concrete work for new walls, wall raises, and access ramps; -- Concrete repair, concrete-channel rehabilitation, and structural concrete demolition; -- Gabion revetment and riprap placement; -- Soil-anchor installation, testing, and shotcrete application; -- In-channel or near-channel construction, including water-control/diversion measures and work-window planning; -- Temporary works, shoring, and protection of existing structures during construction; -- Utility protection, relocation, and restoration; -- Traffic control and maintenance of public, property-owners, and emergency access; -- Concurrent management of multiple construction sites; and -- Planning and providing safe access to constrained work areas through cranes, temporary access systems, or other appropriate means.

description: SOURCES SOUGHT SYNOPSIS / REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) U.S. ARMY CORPS OF ENGINEERS SAN FRANCISCO DISTRICT ***THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT SYNOPSIS / REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI). ADDITIONAL PROJECT DESCRIPTIONS: The work includes maintenance dredging of the federal navigation channels of the projects listed in Table 1 to the required project depths with 1- ft paid over-depth and 1-ft unpaid over-depth. Please refer to Table 1 for disposal site, dredge windows, and other project related information. Upland disposal placement for San Joaquin River and Sacramento River Deep Water Ship Channels (DWSC) are at contractor furnished upland beneficial reuseuse sites or at the various Government-furnished sites located along the channels. If a Government-furnished site is chosen, the and the material shall be pumped to the sites based on various pumping distances and depth of material. Both these projects have water quality and fish entrainment monitoring requirements that need to be performed by a third- party Contractor hired by the either by the Government or the dredging Contractor. For Oakland Harbor and Richmond Harbor, the Contractor is responsible for preparing a light monitoring plan and performing that task during daylight hours where dredging occurs within 250m of eelgrass beds and at monitoring reference sites not influenced by turbidity above ambient for that area. Surveys shall also be conducted prior to and following completion of dredging per SPN�s Light Monitoring Protocol. For Oakland Harbor, in addition to the standard alternative of ocean disposal at SF-DODS or placement at a beneficial use site, approximately 250,000 cubic yards of dredged material may be placed at a nearshore placement site shallow depths (-5 to +5 ft MLLW) near Emeryville Crescent State Marine Reserve in shallow water depths ranging from -5 to +5 ft MLLW. For Redwood City Harbor, the Government is contemplating a contract for dredging services with an anticipated ordering/performance period of up to two years, consisting of a one-year base period and one one-year option period. The final contract type, structure, scope, and period of performance will be determined if and when a solicitation is issued. Acceptance will be based on achieving project depth in 100 percent of the project footprint within the contract period of performance. Anticipated solicitation issuance dates are shown in Table 1. Interested parties must also have the capability and equipment necessary for dredging and disposal of material at the Government-furnished deep ocean disposal site as required by the specific contract. All proposed equipment must be identified including the current location of the dredge plant as part of the response to this Market Research. title: Ireland – Development of residential real estate – Cork City Council Housing Programme 2026-28
description: The Cork City Council Housing Programme 2026-2028 will form part of the City Council’s housing delivery action plan under the Government’s Delivering Homes, Building Communities 2025-2030 (DHBC)1, although this procurement process may include schemes that will be delivered beyond the lifetime of the DHBC. The Government’s DHBC sets out an overall ambition to activate the supply of 300,000 homes over the lifetime of the plan, including an annual average delivery of 12,000 new social homes and 15,000 starter home supports. There are significant targets to be delivered in Cork City and in this regard the Cork City Council Housing Programme 2026-2028 is a major part of the Council’s delivery plan under the DHBC and any subsequent national housing delivery programme. Cork City Council proposes to deliver and facilitate the delivery of social, starter homes and mixed tenure schemes in delivery of its housing programme over the coming years and therefore invites proposals from Candidates which can deliver social, starter homes, or mixed tenure schemes, to include new build construction, conversion of existing residential or non- residential properties, or schemes which form part of a larger development. Starter homes or mixed tenure schemes may include provision for cost-rental delivery in partnership with an Approved Housing Body (AHB).

title: Netherlands – Microscopes – Confocal Microscope
description: The objective of this Procurement Procedure is for Radboud University Medical Center (Radboudumc) to select and contract a single Contractor for the supply, installation, commissioning, training, and maintenance of a Confocal Microscope System for use by RTC Light Microscopy. Through this procurement, Radboudumc intends to expand its existing microscopy infrastructure with a user-friendly and future-proof system capable of delivering rapid, high-resolution three-dimensional (3D) imaging. The intended system shall support the current and future research needs of Radboudumc and contribute to maintaining a state-of-the-art microscopy facility. The microscope system will be installed as a shared research facility within RTC Light Microscopy and will be centrally managed by the UMC. Following installation, commissioning, and the completion of the required user training, the system will be made available to authorised and qualified Radboudumc staff and researchers. The Contracting Authority seeks a reliable and sustainable solution that combines high imaging performance with ease of use, operational continuity, and long-term support throughout the lifecycle of the system.

title: SNPLMA Kalamazoo Fence
description: This intent of this project is to construct approximately 0.5 miles of barbwire fence lines near Kalamazoo Campground on the Ely Ranger District. Construct two barbwire drift fences totaling approximately 0.5 miles in length to exclude active grazing within Kalamazoo Campground. Livestock in the campground presents a safety hazard and has resulted in numerous complaints from the public. In addition, limiting livestock activities within the campground will also extend protection of newly installed recreational infrastructure. This project includes construction of approximately 2,500 feet of new barbwire fence including installation of an estimated four 12-foot wire gates as a lump sum.

title: Z2DA--589A4-25-102, Install Dedicated Pharmacy Air Handler
TECHNOLOGY LICENSING OPPORTUNITY: PBI High-Temperature Hollow Fiber Membranes
description: Polybenzimidazole (PBI) High-Temperature Hollow Fiber Membranes offer a practical way to improve separation efficiency in process environments where standard polymer membranes often lose performance or durability. The platform combines high-temperature operation, chemical resistance and compact hollow-fiber design in a membrane system that can help users recover hydrogen, separate carbon dioxide and process difficult liquid streams with lower energy demand and a smaller equipment footprint than many conventional approaches. Because the fibers are formed from a robust PBI material and engineered with an integrated thin selective layer, the technology is well suited for organizations seeking stronger performance in demanding energy, chemical and water treatment settings. How it Works The membrane works like a selective gate built into a very small hollow strand. A mixed gas or liquid flows across the fiber, and the thin outer layer allows some molecules to pass through more readily than others, while the porous support beneath it gives the fiber strength and a path for transport. The disclosed fabrication process forms that selective layer and support structure in one step, then can add heat treatment or a thin sealing layer to improve stability and sharpen separation performance. Technical Description The polybenzimidazole invention is centered on a method for making asymmetric hollow fiber membranes from polybenzimidazole, a polymer valued for strong thermal and chemical stability. A PBI dope solution and a bore fluid are extruded through a spinneret, then passed through an optional air gap and into a water coagulation bath, which forms a hollow fiber with an integrated selective layer and a porous support structure. The process can produce nearly defect-free selective layers, and the patent states that selective layer thickness can be controlled from about 0.1 to 5 �m, with examples demonstrating thicknesses down to about 160 nm and one example near 0.38 �m. A major technical advantage is control over membrane microstructure and durability. PBI High-Temperature Hollow Fiber Membranes emphasize macrovoid-free fibers, which are important because macrovoids create weak points that can fail under high temperature and pressure. The membranes can be thermally annealed or chemically crosslinked to improve solvent resistance and stability, and a defect-sealing layer can be added to improve selectivity without changing the core fiber architecture. In demonstrated gas-separation modules, the technology showed hydrogen permeance above 100 GPU, with one example reporting 242 GPU at 250 �C and hydrogen/carbon dioxide selectivity of 19.1, while long-term testing in wet syngas with 20 ppm H2S showed stable performance over 40 days. The patent also states that the membranes can operate up to about 400 �C and are suitable for gas, vapor and liquid separations including hydrogen purification, carbon capture, brine treatment and organic solvent separations. Advantages Operates at temperatures that are too demanding for many conventional polymer membranes Resists harsh chemical exposure including steam and sulfur-containing gases compact module design enables smaller equipment footprint easier scaling than ceramic membranes higher throughput without compromising permeability, selectivity or membrane area cost Combines selectivity and structural support in one integrated membrane architecture Supports both gas and liquid separation opportunities across multiple industries Reduces overall hydrogen purification costs Has already been tested in relevant operating environments rather than remaining only a laboratory concept Market Applications Energy and Power generation (hydrogen production, pre-combustion carbon capture, syngas cleanup) Oil and Gas (refining, natural gas processing, produced water treatment) Chemical and Petrochemical Processing (process gas separation, solvent dehydration, feedstream cleanup) Industrial Water and Wastewater (high-salinity brines, water purification, water and acid separation) Advanced Fuels (Fischer-Tropsch processing, fuel conversion, synthesis gas upgrading) Specialty Manufacturing (organic solvent recovery, pharmaceutical and fine chemical separations) Development Status: TRL 5 US Patent No. 10,071,345 LA-UR-26-24561 LANL Tech Partnerships: Unlock the Innovative Potential Los Alamos National Laboratory offers a wide range of cutting-edge technologies and capabilities that may provide your company with a competitive edge in the market and unlock the innovative potential that can enhance, refine, and revolutionize your products. title: V225--VA AIR AMBULANCE BROKER WITH SUPPORTING GROUND TRANSPORTATION VIRTUAL INDUSTRY DAY NOTICE
description: VA AIR AMBULANCE BROKER WITH SUPPORTING GROUND TRANSPORTATION VIRTUAL INDUSTRY DAY NOTICE December 10-11, 2026 Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Veterans Transportation Program (VTP) Network Contracting Office (NCO) 20 1. Purpose The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Transportation Program (VTP), will host an Industry Day to engage with air and ground transportation brokers capable of providing Air Ambulance Broker with Supporting Ground Transportation Services nationwide. This Industry Day is not a request for proposal. It is a market research tool being used to determine potential firms capable of providing the services described herein prior to determining the method of acquisition. The purpose of this session is to: Provide industry with an overview of the upcoming Air Ambulance Broker Services requirement. Offer vendors an opportunity to ask questions and provide feedback prior to release of the solicitation. Support industry�s understanding of VTP�s operational needs, compliance requirements, and contracting expectations as defined within the Performance Work Statement (PWS). 2. Requirement Overview The upcoming procurement will establish multiple-award IDIQ contracts for nationwide fixed-wing and rotary-wing air ambulance broker services, supported by ancillary ground transportation services which refers to transportation services used to transport Veterans between airports, healthcare facilities, Veterans' residences, and other approved destinations. Ground transportation modes may include private vehicles, taxis, rideshare services, wheelchair-accessible vans and shuttles, ambulances, and other specialized transportation services necessary to meet a Veteran's mobility, accessibility, or medical transportation needs. Key highlights include: 24/7/365 availability including holidays Compliance with CAMTS/NAAMTA transport standards Real-time communication and documentation via VA Mandated Transportation Software Quality Control and subcontractor oversight requirements Support for advanced life support, life support, basic life support, critical care transport and stretcher transports 3. The Request for Proposal The Request for Proposal number is 36C26027R0012. The solicitation will result in the award of three (3) to five (5) firm fixed-price MATOCs. The applicable NAICS code is 481211, Nonscheduled Chartered Passenger Air Transportation with a small business size standard of 1,500 employees. 4. Industry Day will be held virtually, on Microsoft Teams, on December 10 � 11, 2026. A hybrid format for this Industry Day is anticipated: December 10, 2026 Morning Session: General overview for all prospective offerors Afternoon Sessions: Optional one-on-one discussions with individual vendors (NTE 50 minutes) December 11, 2026 All Day: Optional one-on-one discussions with individual vendors (NTE 50 minutes hour) Please note that all times for the scheduled sessions will be stated in Pacific Standard Time (PST) 5. Points of Contact (POCs) Contracting (NCO 20): Primary: Wendy Duval @ wendy.duval@va.gov Alternates: Michael Allred @ michael.allred1@va.gov Program Office (VTP): Primary: Tony Guagliardo Alternate: Mindy LaCrone 6. Tentative Agenda Welcome & Introductions Overview of VTP Mission and Needs Air Ambulance PWS Requirements Review Acquisition Strategy & Timeline Vendor Q&A One-on-one Sessions with Interested Offerors 7. Additional Notices This Industry Day is informational only and does not constitute a solicitation or request for proposals. Draft documentation, including the PWS and/or the RFP, may be provided for industry review prior to or during the session. 8. Registration Instructions It is suggested that prime contractors that have both the capabilities and relevant experience to perform most of the required tasks participate. Significant subcontractors may also participate. Interested parties should provide a short (10 Pages) capability statement to the above Contracting POC with the following information: Company Name, Unique Entity ID number (SAM.gov), business size and classification, address and point of contact with phone number & e-mail address. Address your firm's ability to provide nationwide Air Ambulance Broker Services, including fixed-wing, rotary-wing, and ancillary ground transportation services. Describe your process for subcontractor oversight, accreditation status, dispatch and operational capabilities, relevant federal experience providing similar services. Indicate whether attending general session only or requesting a one?on?one breakout Submit any initial questions you may have to help shape agenda topics and ensure the VA has sufficient time to fully answer questions.

title: Belgium – Fire engines – Aankoop 2 Bosbrandwagens Type CCF
description: Hulpverleningszone Noord-Limburg beschikt over grote oppervlakten natuurgebieden (o.a. Nationaalpark Bosland) die elk jaar getroffen worden door natuurbranden (bos, heide,…). Deze ruwe terreinen vereisen gespecialiseerde voertuigen alle terrein om de manschappen, benodigde materiaal en vereiste bluswater ter plaatse te krijgen. Hulpverleningszone Noord-Limburg beschikt reeds over bosbrandvoertuigen type CCF en wil haar vloot uitbreiden met 2 bijkomende bosbrandvoertuigen type CCF 4x4 4.000 l, één voor de nieuwe brandweerpost Peer en één voor brandweerpost Lommel. Beide voertuigen zijn identiek. Het voertuig van brandweerpost Peer dient echter bijkomend uitgerust te worden met een sproeibalk en een systeem voor de dosering van zeep/detergent zodat dit voertuig buiten de winterperiode eveneens gebruikt kan worden voor kleine opdrachten “reinigen wegdek”. In het dossier zal eveneens een bepakkingslijst toegevoegd worden. De aanbieder dient hiervoor de eenheidsprijzen op te geven zodat i.f.v. het resterende budget het voertuig bijkomend uitgerust kan worden met brandbestrijdingsmaterialen. Overige materialen zullen door de Hulpverleningszone Noord-Limburg aangeleverd worden zodat de nodige ruimte voorzien kan worden tijdens de opbouw. De uniformiteit van inrichting van deze nieuwe voertuigen t.o.v. de reeds in gebruik zijnde CCF’s dient behouden te blijven (in samenspraak met de Hulpverleningszone tijdens de opbouw/inrichting). Al het voorgestelde materieel dient nieuw te zijn en elk element dient te voldoen aan de bijzondere interventievoorwaarden. De leverancier dient hiermee rekening te houden bij het voorstellen van het materieel. Het voertuig betreft een bosbrandwagen type CCF voor 4 personen. Het voertuig dient voorzien te zijn van een autoprotectiesysteem met een gereserveerde hoeveelheid water om in geval van nood de bemanning te kunnen beschermen. Het chassis moet van een goedgekeurd en gehomologeerd type zijn, aangepast aan het voertuigontwerp. Deze aanpassing wordt onderbouwd door een gewichtsberekening van het volledige concept, die bij de offerte wordt gevoegd. Bij levering zal het voertuig worden nagewogen. Indien het voertuig niet voldoet aan het vooropgestelde gewicht, kan dit aanleiding geven tot weigering van het product. Het aangeboden voertuig moet van het meest recente commerciële type zijn en geschikt zijn voor rijden en inzet op ruw terrein (oneffenheden in terrein, bospaden, losse zand, heuvels,…). Het voertuig moet op het moment van indiening van de offerte én bij levering volledig voldoen aan de geldende Europese en Belgische regelgeving.

title: Natural Resources Conservation Program Technical Support Services - Camp Darby, Italy
description: Natural Resources Conservation Program Technical Support Services -U.S. Army Garrison Italy, Darby Military Community (DMC), Livorno, Italy 1. Notice Type and Purpose This is a Sources Sought Notice issued by the Department of War (DoW), U.S. Army Garrison Italy, Darby Military Community (DMC), for market-research and acquisition-planning purposes only. The Government is seeking information from capable and interested businesses that can provide non-personal natural-resources conservation program technical support services for DMC in Livorno, Italy. This notice is not a solicitation, request for proposal, request for quotation, invitation for bid, or commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract. The Government will not pay for preparation of responses or reimburse any costs incurred in responding to this notice. Responses will be used solely to conduct market research, assess the availability of qualified sources, support acquisition planning, evaluate potential small-business participation, refine the anticipated scope, evaluate industry interest in an Industry Engagement Day, and determine the final acquisition strategy. The Government seeks responses from all responsible business concerns, including small businesses and businesses participating in applicable socioeconomic programs. 2. Anticipated Requirement The Government is conducting market research to identify firms capable of providing qualified personnel, technical expertise, supervision, transportation, equipment, supplies, and incidental services necessary to provide natural-resources conservation technical support. The anticipated requirement will include on-site and field-based technical support for natural-resources surveys, monitoring, technical analyses, field data collection, technical reporting, forestry, forest nursery and greenhouse operations, mitigation and compensatory projects, landscape assessments, Valutazione d�Incidenza Ambientale (VIncA) and SIncA development, wolf monitoring, pine tortoise scale technical support, regulatory technical support, and Geographic Information System (GIS) support. The final scope, workload, task order structure, labor categories, contract type, period of performance, and individual technical requirements remain subject to refinement after completion of market research and review of submitted capability statements. 2.1 Natural Resources Technical Support The contractor will provide technical support to the Government for natural-resources conservation activities. The contractor will perform work only in response to Government tasking and under the technical direction, review, and oversight of a designated Government employee. The contractor will: Conduct field surveys, monitoring, data collection, analysis, and preparation of draft technical reports addressing: Protected species; Habitats and protected biotopes; Wildlife and ungulate management; Wolf populations; Wetlands and water resources; Forestry and vegetation; Noxious weeds and invasive species; Pine tortoise scale infestation and related forest-health conditions; and Other natural-resources conditions identified by the Government. Monitor wolf populations at Government-designated locations and prepare draft field reports, survey data, maps, photo documentation, and technical observations for Government review. Conduct Government-directed field observation, assessment, monitoring, and technical analysis related to pine tortoise scale infestation within DMC and the Tuscany Region, as applicable. Document observed effects on pine resources and prepare draft technical summaries of Government-provided or publicly available host-nation phytosanitary requirements, regional action-plan measures, and potential natural-resources implications for Government review. Prepare draft natural-resources management plans, plan updates, technical studies, and supporting documentation for Government review. Potential products will include support to: Forest-management planning; Threatened and endangered species management planning; Wetland-management or wetland-restoration planning; Integrated Natural Resources Management Plan updates; and Other Government-identified natural-resources technical products. Prepare draft technical recommendations, field documentation, photo logs, maps, briefing materials, and other natural-resources technical products for Government review. Provide technical support during Government-led inspections, site visits, environmental reviews, and natural-resources project-planning activities. title: TECHNOLOGY LICENSING OPPORTUNITY: SurfGraphPro
description: SurfGraphPro, an AI tool, transforms complex protein structures into an easy-to-analyze format that helps researchers quickly identify binding sites, predict molecular interactions and understand protein behavior with greater speed and scalability than traditional approaches. By combining 3D surface graph representations with advanced machine learning, this technology from Los Alamos National Laboratory reduces the computational burden of protein analysis while preserving the structural detail needed for high-value applications in drug discovery, antibody design, pathogen detection and custom protein engineering. The Challenge: Protein surfaces are extremely complex, three-dimensional structures, and that complexity makes them difficult to analyze using traditional computational approaches. In practice, many existing methods rely on hand-selected biochemical features, expensive calculations or narrow task-specific models that do not generalize well to new questions. As a result, researchers can face slow runtimes, limited scalability and incomplete insight when trying to identify binding sites, predict molecular interactions or understand broader protein behavior across large sets of proteins. These limitations can make it difficult to move quickly from protein structure data to useful predictions in areas such as drug discovery, antibody design, pathogen detection and protein engineering. Problems Solved: SurfGraphPro solves these problems by converting protein surfaces into a graph-based representation that preserves both the physical shape of the surface and the biochemical information carried by surface-exposed amino acids. This tool gives machine learning models a more efficient and flexible way to process protein structures without requiring repeated manual feature engineering or highly specialized analysis pipelines for each new use case. By reducing computational burden while keeping the key structural details needed for prediction, SurfGraphPro makes it possible to analyze proteins more quickly, at larger scale and across a wider range of applications. This approach includes identifying likely binding sites, estimating molecular compatibility, supporting drug screening efforts, improving antibody and protein design workflows, and enabling other protein-focused prediction tasks where speed, scalability and adaptability matter. Key Advantages: Helps turn complex protein structures into information computers can use more easily Speeds up protein analysis compared with older approaches Reduces the amount of manual feature engineering needed Preserves important details about both protein shape and chemical properties Supports multiple uses, including drug discovery, antibody design and pathogen detection Offers a flexible platform that can be adapted to different protein-related tasks Market Applications: Pharmaceuticals and Biotechnology (drug discovery, target screening, protein optimization) Biologics and Antibody Development (antibody engineering, binding analysis, therapeutic design) Diagnostics and Infectious Disease (pathogen detection, biomarker analysis, assay development) Agricultural Biotechnology (protein analysis, crop trait research, bio-based product development) Materials and Industrial Science (protein-mineral interaction studies, polymer compatibility, bio-inspired materials) Research Tools and Software (protein modeling, computational biology, prediction platforms) Development Status: TRL 3 US Patent pending LA-UR-26-23589 LANL Tech Partnerships: Unlock the Innovative Potential Los Alamos National Laboratory offers a wide range of cutting-edge technologies and capabilities that may provide your company with a competitive edge in the market and unlock the innovative potential that can enhance, refine, and revolutionize your products. LANL�s licensing program focuses on moving inventions developed by our researchers to commercial innovations. Patented and patent pending inventions and copyrighted software are available to existing and start-up companies through exclusive and non-exclusive licensing agreements. For specific discussions, please contact licensing@lanl.gov. title: Hazardous Waste Removal, Disposal, and Recycling at Diego Garcia
description: For the Removal and Off-Site Disposal of Hazardous and Recyclable Wastes Located Diego Garcia Who � Defense Logistics Agency (hereinafter DLA) on behalf of US Military activities located at Diego Garcia in the British Indian Ocean Territory. What � DLA has a 5-year contract requirement for the removal and off-site disposal of regulated and non-regulated wastes generated by US military operations. Wastes will be properly packaged and loaded onto Cargo Transport Units (CTU) for marine vessel transport to the US or EU for disposal and/or recycling. Wastes include but are not limited to regulated flammables, corrosives, toxics, and recyclable batteries and automotive fluids. The awarded company will: Identify preferred waste disposal and recycling facilities, having them pre-vetted for inclusion on the DLA Qualified Facilities List (QFL) at https://www.dla.mil/Disposition-Services/Offers/Hazardous-Waste-Disposal/Qualified-Facilities-List/, Prepare Basel Convention and other documents for transboundary movements as applicable, Prepare shipping documents for transportation to/in the Host Nation where disposal and recycling is completed, Ensure all wastes are packaged according to IMDG Code and other applicable transportation laws and regulations, Prior to shipment, with a US Government representative, perform pre-shipment inspection of all containers to verify suitability for transport via marine vessel, Transport loaded CTUs to pier side transfer facility and oversee loading onto contractor chartered marine transport vessel, Oversee DLA Qualified Transporter contractor chartered marine transport vessel logistics en route, Oversee unloading of CTUs from marine transport vessel and transport via ground to destination DLA Qualified Facility, Ensure all wastes are properly disposed or recycled, and Provide DLA with supporting documentation to certify tracking of waste and completion of work. Removal quantities will vary. Current inventory exceeds 168 tons in 16 loaded CTUs. A DLA Qualified Facility is a treatment, storage, disposal and/or recycling facility that has demonstrated to DLA a sufficient historical record of safety, operational, and regulatory compliance standards. Interested companies must be qualified and credentialed to handle hazardous material and hazardous waste (HM/HW) at both the loading and unloading locations. Interested companies should indicate whether they can provide initial packaging services to place waste in UN rated drums and other containers purchased by the US Government, then loaded into CTUs for marine vessel transportation, as well as charter the marine vessel for transportation to final destination. Where � Waste will be removed from the US military base, Diego Garcia, and transported to the US or EU for disposal/recycling. When � Removals will be performed annually over a 5-year performance period having a 30-month base period and 30-month option period. Why � DLA Disposition Services is requiring responsible disposal and recycling of regulated and non-regulated hazardous and recyclable wastes in support of operations at Diego Garcia. Submit information and any questions to kayla.desvoignes@dla.mil and daniel.schuemann@dla.mil with "Request for Information Hazardous Waste Diego Garcia" in the subject line.

title: Syväkeräysastioiden vuosihuollot / VAV
description: Syväkeräysastioiden vuosihuollot / VAV Tilaajan tavoitteena on hankkia joustava ja luotettava yhteistyökumppani Vantaalla sijaitsevien VAV-konsernin omistamien vuokratalokohteiden syväkeräysjätepisteiden vuosihuoltoihin. VAV-konserni omistaa noin 12 000 vuokra-asuntoa, joissa asuu noin 19 000 asukasta. Tarkempi luettelo sopimuksen piiriin kuuluvista syväkeräyskohteista on tarjouspyynnön liitteenä olevassa kohdeluettelossa. Sopimus ei sisällä määräostovelvoitetta, eikä Tilaaja sitoudu tarjouspyynnössä tai hankintailmoituksessa esitettyihin arvioihin hankintamääristä. Työtilauksiin voi sisältyä myös tarvikehankintoja ja muita työn suorittamiseen liittyviä palveluhankintoja. Tavoitteiden saavuttamisen edellytykset on kerrottu tarkemmin tarjouspyynnön ESPD-lomakkeella, hankinnan kohteen kriteerit -osiossa sekä hankintailmoituksen liitteissä. Hankintapäätöksen tekoperusteena on kokonaistaloudellinen edullisuus pisteytyksen mukaisesti, jossa maksimipisteet ovat 1000 pistettä. Tarjoajan on annettava tarjous kaikista tarjouslomakkeen töistä. Mikäli Tarjoaja ei ole tarjonnut kaikkia tarjouslomakkeeseen eriteltyjä töitä, tulkitaan tarjous puutteelliseksi. Puutteellinen tarjous hylätään. Tarjoajan kannalta huomioitavaa on myös se, että tarjottujen töiden ja hintojen tulee sisältää kaikki tässä tarjouspyynnössä, hankintasopimusluonnoksessa ja palvelukuvauksessa määritellyt kriteerit. Hankintasopimus syntyy vasta kirjallisen sopimuksen allekirjoittamisella, selonottoneuvottelujen jälkeen. Angelehnt an die Erfahrungen aus der Flaniermeile Volksdorf würde die Reduzierung des Parksuchverkehrs zu einer Verkehrsberuhigung und somit zu einer verbesserten Aufenthaltsqualität im Projektgebiet führen. Es können beispielsweise Elemente wie mehr Parkbänke, Pflanzbeete, kleine Spielinseln für Kinder oder Nutzungsmöglichkeiten durch Außengastronomie installiert werden, die zu einer Belebung des Straßenzuges und zu einer signifikanten Verbesserung der Aufenthaltsqualität sowie der Verweilzeit vor Ort beitragen. Ziel ist die Umsetzung der Planung für einen Verkehrsberuhigten Geschäftsbereich, ggf. mit der Entwicklung verschiedener denkbarer Untervarianten. Als Bestandteil im Planungsverlauf ist die Beteiligung der Öffentlichkeit vorgesehen. Das Format und der jeweilige Umfang der Beteiligung müssen noch abgestimmt werden. Dennoch sollte es für die Öffentlichkeit die Möglichkeit geben, sich aktiv in den Gestaltungsprozess vor Ort mit einbringen zu können, damit die Bürgerinnen und Bürger zum Beispiel an der Positionierung von Sitzbänken oder grüner Inseln im Straßenzug aktiv mitarbeiten können.
